summary: Run 39874053570 of wasm-installed-c.yml was the single dispatch admitted by FS-GG/.github#4710 comment 6352823677, at 32b6192 (admission #745, preceded by precondition #744; reset by #746 to c1b1a23, 11 min after the conclusion). Artifact 12467901371, sha256:068b60c2.... Independent acceptance and fdev acceptance (comment 6354169215): FAILED-AS-EVIDENCE, 9/27; the admission is spent, with no re-run. Established hosted: all 25 managed groups that ran were contained under the real pinned owner (d846dbe1), including groups 7-25 for the first time (observed-empty-removed, no escapes or residue), which retires the named owner-launch risk. The unit and package readbacks matched (Azure mirror used), all 17 acquisitions matched their pins, the ProviderTool restore and build worked (the #742 fix), and the checker returned source-passed. Chromium passed 9/9. Measured with #744's recording: setup 63.1 s of 840 s; installed 90.3 s of 1230 s (stopped at Firefox); checker 66.6 s; sequence 153.5 s. pids.peak was at most 188 per group, with the unit at 189 of 6144. The unit's cumulative memory.peak was 5.69 GiB of 12 GiB, mostly page cache. There were 0 oom_kill and 0 pids.events max events, so a resource cause is ruled out. CPU pressure was not recorded. First cause (a product defect, FS-GG/FS.GG.Game#727): the first Firefox case went from preparing to refused, with 'Refused: DeadlineExpired'. FS.GG.Wasm.Contracts 0.3.0 sets sc2Limits.MaximumDeadlineMilliseconds = 250 with Deadline = EndToEndFromEnqueue, and Wasm.Browser 0.3.0 arms that timer when it posts to a freshly created module Worker that loads an unbundled Fable graph (about 38 modules; about 252 ms to fetch in the trace). Firefox: 0 passed, 1 failed, 8 not run (--max-failures=1). WebKit: 0 of 9 run. The same case passed in a local 24-CPU rehearsal. It is one sample of a race against a fixed budget, so it is not proven deterministic. The producer's package-consumer Playwright config has no projects, so it runs Chromium only. Lessons: a fixed wall-clock deadline that includes cold Worker boot is a cross-browser and host-speed hazard, and a fast local rehearsal can hide it. Qualify every browser family upstream, with cold loads under a hosted-like CPU limit. Note that Playwright labels tests not run after max-failures as 'skipped'. fdev's direction: the policy deadline bounds policy work only, and Worker readiness gets its own bounded timeout and refusal. Path to run 3: Game#727 fixed and new FS.GG.Wasm.* versions published; the receiver re-pinned in a Workspace.Template patch release; a three-browser cold-load timing check; then a new admission. The Done-when receiver is the current published Workspace.Template carrying the fix (0.19.2 today).
title: Installed-C run 2: 9/27; Chromium passed; Firefox refused by the 250 ms EndToEndFromEnqueue policy deadline (FS.GG.Game#727)
